blocks.text: **The problem.** Like Unique Paths, but some cells hold an **obstacle** (`1` in `obstacleGrid`) that the robot can't enter. Count the paths from the top-left to the bottom-right moving only right or down.

blocks.alt: A 3 by 3 grid with an obstacle in the middle. The obstacle cell has 0 paths. The bottom-right corner adds the cell above it and the cell to its left, 1 + 1 = 2: one path around the top right, one around the bottom left.

elements.text: an obstacle has 0 paths, so it adds nothing to its neighbours

blocks.code:
obstacleGrid = [[0,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,0]]  ->  2
obstacleGrid = [[0,1],[0,0]]              ->  1
obstacleGrid = [[1]]                      ->  0   (the start is blocked)

blocks.text: Same recurrence as Unique Paths — paths from above plus paths from the left — with one rule: a blocked cell has **0** paths. That also fixes the edges automatically: along the top row, once a cell is blocked, every cell after it has 0 paths, because the only way in was through the obstacle. If the start itself is blocked, the answer is 0.

blocks.caption: Open cells add the paths from above and from the left; blocked cells stay at 0.

blocks.text: **Time O(m · n), space O(n).** A blocked start sets `row[0] = 0` on the first row, and it stays 0.

blocks.alt: Memoized recursion: O(m · n) time, O(m · n) space. Table: O(m · n) time, O(m · n) space. One row: O(m · n) time, O(n) space.

items: **The start or the end is blocked** — 0.
**An obstacle on the top row** — every cell to its right on that row has 0 paths.
**Unique Paths III** — visit every empty cell exactly once: backtracking, not DP.
